The plateau shattered. The posts spread like wildfire across social media feeds—it was primetime, just before the end of the workday—and the viewer count instantly jumped from two hundred thousand to two hundred and fifty thousand. Online media bots latched onto the event and began churning out news about a provocative stream by "the most innovative business coach of our generation." A woman, no less!

Now three hundred and fifty thousand people from all over the world were watching, liking, sharing, and paying real dollars to ask Freya a question. Three hundred and sixty. Three hundred and seventy. Every new thousand took Freya's breath away. And then it was time to answer.

The key was not to let this chat with her followers turn into a group Tinder date.

*"Do you have kids?"* a stranger asked. *"How do you succeed when you've got four of them?"*

Freya wanted to answer, *"You don't."* But first of all, stay-at-home moms made up forty-eight percent of her audience, so it was a sore subject. And second, you couldn't say that to a follower who had most likely scraped together those fifty bucks out of her kids' lunch money. So Freya went with a polite, pre-rehearsed answer.

"Everyone defines success for themselves," she said. "If you've always dreamed of being a mom or a dad, then your children *are* your capital. The key is to stick to your investment strategy and not hand your capital over to unproven funds."

*"Are you married?"* someone asked, after donating the minimum five dollars.

Questions like that Freya now left unanswered. Luckily, the stream of more interesting (and pricier!) questions flushed all the cheap provocations down the toilet.

Besides, her joke had landed. The chat was thrilled, and the viewer count kept climbing: a clip of her answer had already gone viral on Twitter. But fame comes with responsibility—the questions took a sharp turn into group-Tinder-date territory.

changes.before: you can't say that to a follower
changes.after: you couldn't say that to a follower
